entities.name: Primary biliary cholangitis
observations: Formerly called primary biliary cirrhosis; histological staging is commonly assessed with Scheuer or Ludwig systems.

entities.name: Canals of Hering loss
observations: Canals of Hering density is reduced early in primary biliary cholangitis and decreases further with increasing histological stage in human biopsy cohorts.
Reduced canals of Hering density correlates inversely with fibrosis, bile-duct loss, and hepatitis activity.
Near-complete periportal loss can occur in minimally inflamed or nearly normal-appearing biopsies, indicating an early lesion.
Focal c-Kit-positive canals of Hering-like clusters or strings may remain detectable in advanced disease; marker-based detection is method-dependent.

entities.name: PMID:25430494
observations: In 62 untreated primary biliary cholangitis biopsies, canals of Hering density was reduced in mild disease and further reduced with increasing histological stage; counts inversely correlated with fibrosis and bile-duct loss.

entities.name: PMID:22911653
observations: In 10 patients with minimal-change primary biliary cholangitis, K19-positive canals of Hering were markedly depleted despite nearly normal or minimally inflamed routine histology.

entities.name: PMID:16963314
observations: In 53 primary biliary cholangitis specimens stratified by Ludwig stage, c-Kit marking canals of Hering was absent in early stages and focal in advanced stages; CK7 changes tracked stage, whereas CK19 did not.
